title: Size It Right
briefing: Steady Orchard Foods and jumpy Kestrel Air. Use the ticket's "risk if stopped" figure to keep the risk on every trade at about 1% of your portfolio.
objective: Size each position from your stop: shares = (portfolio × risk %) ÷ (entry − stop).
debrief: Orchard Foods climbed calmly. Kestrel Air swung hard, and on day 16 it gapped down about 10% when part of its fleet was grounded. Players who sized Kestrel from their stop held only a small position, so even the gap past their stop cost little. Anyone who put most of their cash into Kestrel took a large drawdown in a single day.

news.headline: Kestrel Air grounds part of its fleet for inspections
news.body: Kestrel Air has grounded a third of its planes for safety inspections and canceled many flights.

bonus.text: Keep your worst drop within your plan's maximum loss
